name: Medicine
description: Human physiology, anatomy, pathology and pharmacology explained for education — never individual medical advice.

figureTypes.name: Physiology plot
figureTypes.description: Relationships such as pressure, flow or concentration over time, from cited equations or data.

figureTypes.name: Pathway diagram
figureTypes.description: Signaling, metabolic or feedback pathways as labeled boxes and arrows.

figureTypes.name: Anatomical schematic
figureTypes.description: Simplified, clearly labeled schematic; must say it is not to scale and cite the anatomy it follows.

conventions: Use the units clinicians use and state them every time: blood pressure in millimetres of mercury (mm Hg), heart rate in beats per minute (bpm), volumes in millilitres (mL) or litres (L).
Give normal ranges with their source and population; never present a single value as 'normal' for everyone.
Write drug names as international nonproprietary names (generic names), never brand names.

safetyNotes: This book is for education only. It does not give medical advice, diagnosis or treatment, and it must not be used to make decisions about anyone's health. Ask a qualified health professional about any medical question.
restrictedDetail: Individual treatment, dosing, titration or tapering instructions
Ways to obtain prescription drugs without a prescription
Methods of self-harm, overdose thresholds, or lethal doses
Instructions that would let someone culture, enhance or spread a pathogen
draftingNotes: Every clinical statement needs a citation to a textbook, guideline or peer-reviewed source; mark simplifications explicitly.
Describe how physiology works in general; do not tell the reader what to do about their own body.
